title: A Millennium of UK Business Cycles: Insights from Structural VAR Analysis - Replication Spec
hypothesis: The source and propagation of UK business cycle shocks changed over time: pre-1900 supply-driven/stagflationary (output and inflation negative comovement) vs post-1900 demand-driven (positive comovement), with monetisation having large real effects in 16th-17th c. shifting to inflationary thereafter.
data_sources: A millennium of macroeconomic data, Ryland et al. 2018 (Thomas and Dimsdale), updated to 2022
Schmelzing 2020 long-term real interest rate for DFM
sample: Baseline 3-variable annual UK macro data in first differences: GDP per capita (real GDP at market prices per capita; England only 1271-1700, UK 1700-; correlation of England and UK GDP growth 1700-onwards printed), CPI variation (cost of living England 1271-1869, UK 1870-), Money M0 per capita (merged M0 series 1833-; M3 estimate variation 1271-1832). Broad money M4x used in robustness. First 50 observations used as training sample. Sample sizes (N) not printed as counts.
method: 1. Sample: Annual data 1271-2022. Use Y_t = {Delta y_t, Delta p_t, Delta m_t} = first differences of log GDP per capita, log CPI, log M0 per capita. First 50 observations as pre-sample training for OLS prior.

2. Model: Time-varying VAR with stochastic volatility and fat tails, lag length P=2: Y_t = c_t + sum_{j=1}^{P} b_{j,t} Y_{t-j} + Sigma_t^{1/2} e_t, e~N(0,1). Coefficients random walk Phi_t = Phi_{t-1} + Q^{1/2} eta_t where Phi_t=vec([c_t,b_{j,t}]). Covariance factored Sigma_t = A_t^{-1} H_t A_t^{-1}', non-zero elements of A_t random walk, H_t diagonal with sigma_{i,t}^2 * 1/lambda_{i,t}, ln sigma_{i,t}^2 = ln sigma_{i,t-1}^2 + g_i^{1/2} z_t, lambda_{i,t} scale mixture of normals yielding orthogonalised residuals A_t u_t ~ t(0, sigma_{i,t}, v_{lambda,i}).

3. Priors: phi_0 from OLS on pre-sample; sigma_0^2 from diagonal of v^{ols}; A_0 ~ N(a^{ols}, V(a^{ols})) diagonal V = 10*|a^{ols}|; Q_0 ~ IW(Qbar_0,T0) Qbar_0=var(phi^{OLS})*1e-4; S_{i,0} ~ IW(Sbar_i,K_i) Sbar diagonal = a^{ols}*1e-3; sigma_i^2 ~ IG(1e-4/2,1/2); p(lambda_k)=prod Gamma(1,v_{lambda,k}), p(v_{lambda,k}) ~ Gamma(v0,2) with v0=20.

4. Estimation: Gibbs sampling cycling 8 conditional posteriors: G(lambda_{i,t}|Psi), G(v_{lambda,i}|lambda), G(g_{i,t}|Psi), G(sigma_{i,t}^2|Psi), G(A_t|Psi), G(Phi_t|Psi), G(Q|Psi), G(Q_A|Psi) using Carter-Kohn 2005 forward-filter backward-sampler for Phi_t, Jacquier-Polson-Rossi 2004 Metropolis-Hastings for H_t, block-diagonal state-space for A_t, Geweke 1993 gamma for lambda and Random Walk MH for v_{lambda}.

5. Identification: Business cycle shock = VAR innovation explaining largest share of forecast error variance (FEV) of Delta y_t at horizon K=1. Decompose Sigma=Omega Omega', Omega=tilde Omega Q with tilde Omega Cholesky and Q orthonormal rotation. Structural MA Y_t = B(L)Omega epsilon_t. Maximize e1'[sum_{k=0}^{K} sum_{j=0}^{k-1} B_j tilde Omega Q1 Q1' tilde Omega' B_j']e1 s.t. Q1'Q1=1. Normalized to unit standard deviation. Equivalent to shock dominating business-cycle frequencies 1.5-8 years (Angeletos et al 2020). Compute IRFs cumulated over 5-year horizon, FEVDs, conditional vs unconditional stochastic volatilities. Report medians and 68% credible sets.

6. Extensions: 4-variable VAR with nominal interest rate (post-1700 only) with sign restrictions to decompose pure aggregate demand vs money supply shocks; Robustness with M4 per capita, aggregate non-per-capita variables, Dynamic Factor Model with 11 variables (real wages, GDP deflator, CPI, exports, commodity prices, GDP, GDP per capita, M4, share prices, dollar rate, real rate) in first differences except rate, unbalanced panel, r-star as 5-year-ahead forecast of real rate.
